name: Dev-via-spec Reviewer Approved → Challenger Handoff
description: When the dev-via-spec-reviewer emits decide(action=approved), the completeness gate has passed. This rule fires on that signal and spawns the dev-via-spec-challenger specialist for adversarial probing. The challenger looks for falsifiable concerns the completeness checklist would not catch (decomposition coarseness, scope creep, missing failure modes). R3.3 of the ADR-031 phasing.

on_enter.subject: agent.task.dev-via-spec-challenge
on_enter.prompt: The dev-via-spec reviewer approved a plan for completeness. Reviewer loop id: $entity.id (passed as prior_loop_id in your task properties). Call read_loop_result with that loop id to read the reviewer's verdict; the verdict's reason field summarises the plan that was approved. Probe for falsifiable concerns per your `20-failure-classes.md`. If no actionable concerns surface, call decide(action=accept). Otherwise call decide(action=concerns_raised, reason="<bullet list of concerns with evidence pointers>").

metadata.pattern: adversarial challenger (ported from SemSpec QA-as-adversary, separated into a distinct role per ADR-031)
metadata.cross_grounding_caveat: Same caveat as rule 01: the challenger reads only the prior reviewer loop. The plan content is reachable via the reviewer's decide reason field (which summarises what was approved), but the original planner content is not directly addressable without rule-engine property-passthrough. R3.3's challenger persona is defensive — it probes the plan as summarised by the reviewer. R3.4 or an upstream improvement should add forward-propagation.
